text:
sam: Hey infra — onboarding a new tenant (Account: 987654321234) in eu-west-1. We need quota increases for p5 and g5 instance families + ENI/vCPU headroom. Pilot starts next Wed, so want tickets opened today. Requesting: 
- p5.24xlarge: 4 On-Demand (prefer reserved if possible)
- g5.12xlarge: 8 On-Demand
- ENIs: increase to 200 per AZ
- vCPU soft limit bump to cover the instances above
Reason: production-facing model serving (low-latency, large KV cache). Can someone start the AWS quota requests? :pray:

lee: Thanks — can you confirm whether those are spread across two AZs or single AZ? Also do we need placement groups or LaunchTemplates pinned to specific subnets? AWS often asks for AZ distribution.

sam: Spread across 2 AZs (eu-west-1a + eu-west-1b). No special placement groups to start, we'll use mix of subnets. Launch templates ready, tagging scheme: Team=infra, Project=pilot-quant, CostCenter=AI.

maria: FYI — p5 availability in eu-west-1 has been patchy historically. Might be safer to request p4d as fallback in the same ticket. Also ask for a soft limit for G5s to be higher than requested so we can burst.

raj: I can file the requests. Need the org ID and payer account email for the support case. Also, do we want Dedicated Hosts or default tenancy?

sam: Use Org ID: o-0abcde1234, payer: billing@redwood.ai. Default tenancy ok for pilot. If AWS pushes back we can explore Dedicated Hosts later.

raj: Opening quota cases now. Creating separate service-quotas requests for EC2 instance limits and ENI/vCPU limits. Will also add p4d as a fallback: p4d.24xlarge: 2.

aws-quotas-bot: Case created: #CASE-202508-12345 - EC2 quota increase (p5/g5/p4d + ENI). Status: Pending AWS account team review.

lee: When you file, include the expected throughput and uptime SLA (pilot: 95% of traffic in peak 8 hours, target <100ms tail latency). AWS sometimes wants traffic and CPU utilization estimates. Also mention we are a production customer with reserved capacity plans coming.

sam: Copy for justification: "Production pilot for Redwood customer (internal code: PILOT-QUANT). Serving large open models with KV cache. Expected peak: ~3.5k reqs/min, avg 120 tokens/req, modeled token throughput ~420k tokens/min. Need p5 for memory and latency constraints; g5 for cost-sensitive burst capacity." 

maria: Good. Also add note about security/compliance: private VPC, no public IPs on instances, KMS-managed keys. That speeds approvals for enterprise requests.

raj: Submitted the EC2 instance quota tickets and ENI/vCPU limit request. Support links: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=CASE-202508-12345 (internal only). Case description includes org ID and pilot justification.

raj: Quick AWS CLI snippet to check current quotas if anyone wants to verify before provisioning:
```
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-1216C47A --region eu-west-1
```
(replace quota-code with the one for instance limits you want to inspect)

oncall-bot: Reminder: file change request for VPC route modifications and security group rules before any instance provisioning. Link to change template: https://redwood-ops.internal/changes

aws-quotas-bot: Case update: CASE-202508-12345 — AWS account team responded, asking for AZ-level distribution and confirmation of projected spend. Please reply within 24h to avoid delays.

sam: Replying with AZ distribution and estimated monthly spend: ~$28k for pilot (on-demand), will convert to reserved/dedicated if pilot succeeds. I added that to the case comments.

raj: AWS responded and provisionally approved g5 quota but p5 is pending TAM review. They've asked for a short call; I'll schedule with the AWS account team for tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

maria: Thanks — if TAM asks, have the model memory footprint numbers ready (per-instance GPU memory usage + KV cache sizes). Also have a fallback plan: we can degrade to g5-only but will need to decrease batch sizes to keep latency.

sam: Noted. I'll prepare the memory/throughput appendix and share in the case. If we don't get p5 approved in 48h, plan B: use p4d + higher g5s and shift noncritical traffic to lower-cost hosts.

raj: Filed a follow-up comment on the case with the appendix and linked the scheduled TAM call. Case now: #CASE-202508-12345 (Pending TAM). I'll ping here after the call. :phone:

aws-quotas-bot: Case update: CASE-202508-12345 — g5 increase approved (eu-west-1). p5 increase escalated to TAM review. ENI/vCPU request under review.

sam: Awesome — thanks all. Moving account numbers and billing details to a private thread. Will close this public thread once we have final approvals. :white_check_mark:
